PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349


APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES§

BEFORE THE

PUBLIC UTILITY

COMMISSION 

OF TEXAS 


JOHN M. BURROW’S
APPEAL OF SOAH ORDER NO. 25
TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS
John M. Burrow ("Mr. Burrow, me , my, I, mine, etc.”), a pro se intervenor, on behalf of himself and the 179 aligned directly affected landowners who joined the Motion for Immediate Remedy and Relief Due to Applicants' Failure to Provide Required Notice, timely files this appeal of State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”) Order No. 25 (59475-5331): Denying Mr. Burrow’s Motion for Relief for Failure to Provide Required Notice.
 In support of this appeal, Mr. Burrow respectfully shows as follows:

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This appeal is not a request for special treatment. It is a request for equal treatment.
Mr. Burrow brings this appeal because SOAH Order No. 25 denies owners of over 1,300 directly affected properties, including Mr. Burrow’s property, the relief due them in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5), due to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s (“Oncor’s”) and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s (“LCRA TSC’s”)(collectively, “Applicants’”)  failure to comply with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(4). SOAH Order No. 25 also denies relief due David and Amy Hillock, the relief due them in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5), due to Applicants’ failure to obtain current county tax rolls, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3).
If upheld, SOAH Order No. 25 would establish an expansive precedent that would allow future Applicants to deny greater and greater numbers of landowners their right and duty to be a knowledgeable, prepared, and effective party to any future application for certificate of convenience and necessity (“CCN”). This potential new standard would allow applicants to hold one early public meeting, only inviting a small number of landowners, and then using that single public meeting to deny large numbers of property owners the same right to a public meeting and opportunity for public input, as is clearly required by 16 Tex. Admi Code 22.52.(a).(4). If allowed to stand, SOAH Order No. 25 the PUC would be opening the door and sanctioning easy abuse of notice and public participation by future applicants.
Additionally, upholding SOAH Order No. 25 would establish a second expansive precedent that would allow Applicants to use whatever county tax roll is convenient to their purposes, rather than the current county tax roll, with best-available, current property ownership data, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(3).
Upholding SOAH Order No. 25 would circumvent the interests of directly affected landowners in favor of the subject and future applicants. Other than the sister Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP), 765-kV, Import Path 1, Mr. Burrow has found no other examples for this vast and sizeable violation of the public involvement process of and subsequent denial of rights of full participation and due process of over 1,300 directly affected property owners.
Accordingly, Mr. Burrow respectfully files this appeal of SOAH Order No. 25 and requests the Commission overrule SOAH Order No. 25 and grant his request for relief.

FAILURE TO PROVIDE PUBLIC MEETINGS 
          FOR AFFECTED PROPERTY OWNERS
Applicants held three, identical public meetings in June 2025. They invited owners of 2,809 affected properties to their choice of any of the three identical public meetings. (59475-65, p. 29)
From the notices and public meetings, Applicants collected public input regarding features of individual noticed affected properties and the community values the noticed landowners.
Based on that public input, the Applicants made drastic changes to their proposed routes, impacting 1,300-1,400 new properties and even expanding their study area. (59475-5132, p. 4)
The total length of route link segments presented at the public meeting was 800-900 miles.
After the public meeting, the Applicants removed approximately 140 miles of route links, due to information collected. They also modified approximately 68 miles of route links, impacting new properties, and the Applicants added totally new links 353 miles of, also impacting more new properties. (59475-5261, p. 6) and (59475-5274, p. 8)
The total length of route link segments included in the application was about 1,162 miles. (59475-5274, p. 5)
The Applicants sent notice of application to about 4,200 owners of directly affected properties. These 1,300 to 1,400 owners of property were not provided notice and afforded an opportunity for public meeting or the opportunity to provide public input, including community values, which the Applicants rely heavily on in their route location analysis. (59475-109, Att. 12)
These 1,300 to 1,400 owners of property were not provided notice and afforded an opportunity for public meeting or the opportunity to provide public input, including community values, and they are due their full, day-for-day relief of over 200 days, as provided by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5),

FAILURE TO NOTIFY CURRENT LANDOWNERS OF APPLICATION
Applicants are required to obtain current county tax rolls for use in mailing notices of application to all affected landowners. (16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(4)
David and Amy Hillock purchased their Burnet County property on November 3, 2025.
Applicants mailed the March 26, 2026, notice of application to the previous owner, Vincet and Carol Eads. (59475-109, Att. 12)
Burnet Central Appraisal District continually updates changes in property ownership in their current tax roll, typically being no more than one month behind. The Applicants did not utilize the current Burnet County tax roll for their March 26, 2026, mailings, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).
Either the Applicant used a tax roll previous obtained, which had become outdated, or they did not properly request a copy of the “current” tax roll from the Burnet Central Appraisal District.
The Hillocks were not notified of the filing of the Application and have still not been notified as of this date, even though they telephoned the Applicants and posted notice on the 59475 PUC Docket Interchange. As such they are due their full, day-for-day relief of over 70 days, as provided by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

APPLICANTS DID NOT COORDINATE WITH PUC
The Applicants were aware that public involvement might become an issue and in late 2025, and they had internal communications about the possibility of additional public meetings. (59475-5340, pp. 8-10)
The Applicants did not coordinate with PUC regarding the need for or possibility of conducting additional public meetings due to the expansive route link additions and modifications made after the June 2025 public meetings. They appear to have made the decision in a vacuum to provide benefit to their own efforts rather than engage the public as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(4). (59475-5340)
In a breach of public trust, the Applicant kept the newly added route links, and expansive link modifications, secret from the public until they filed their application on March 26, 2026. (59475-5308, p. 6)
At this time, it is unknown whether the Applicants even made the PUC aware of the expansive route link additions and modifications made after the June 2025 public meetings. If the PUC knew of the tremendous expansion, they should have required notification and additional public involvement, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(4). 
If the Applicant kept the newly added route links, and expansive link modifications, secret from the PUC as well as public, the totality of the breach of trust would be incredibly egregious. 
All impacted landowners are due their full, day-for-day relief, as provided by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

PURA § 37.057 IS NOT IN CONFLICT WITH 16 TEX. ADMIN. CODE § 22.25(a)
There is perfect harmony and there is no conflict between PURA 37.057 and 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.52.(a). 
The legislation provided PURA § 37.057 with a self-healing remedy expressly for the anticipated future inability of the Commission to always meet the deadline to approve or deny an application for CCN. PURA § 37.057 provides protection for the public, when longer review timeframes are necessary, as is the case here for 59475, while also providing all parties protection by directing that they may seek relief in a Travis County Court.)
Commissioner Gleeson committed in testimony during the April 1, 2026, Texas Senate Committee on Business and Commerce hearing that:
“We are never going to sacrifice figuring out what is in the public interest in making the right decision for expediency, so I view the 180 days as a signal from the legislature that they, that you all, would like us to get this done as quickly as possible, but we are never going to make a decision that is not fully informed just to meet a 180- day timeline.”
(https://senate.texas.gov/videoplayer.php?vid=22651&lang=en) 
(April 1, 2026) ---- Beginning at timestamp 4:19:08 ----
These 1,300 to 1,400 owners of property were not provided notice and afforded an opportunity for public meeting or the opportunity to provide public input, including community values, and they are due the full relief of over 200 days, AND the Hillocks, who were not notified of the filing of the Application and have still not been notified as of this date, are due the full relief of over 70 days, both as provided by 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

IV. PRAYER
The required public notice and full opportunity to participate denied to a very large number of landowners, by SOAH Order No. 25, would establish a precedent that would allow future CCN applicants to easily game the system and deny property owners a right to intervene and fully engage in a manner they might consider advantageous to their application efforts. Even if an innocent “oversight” the result is the same, directly affected property owners were not notified and SAOH Order No. 25 allows that practice to continue, unchecked. If left to stand, 59182 SOAH Order No. 25 would be an unjust standard.
Accordingly, Mr. Burrow appeals SOAH Order No. 25 and respectfully requests that the Commission:
Do not permit this landmark appeal to be set aside or to be ignored due to any procedural technicalities or failings.
OVERRULE SOAH Order No. 25 and GRANT the full remedy and relief requested in in my motion, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).
COMPEL the Applicant to obtain proper current county tax rolls and notify all affected landowners not notified in their original March 26, 2026, notification of application. We know of a 2025 landowner in Bell County, similar to the Hillocks, who was not notified. The number of total non-notified landowners is unknown at this time, and this recurring lack of due process must be remedied.
COMPEL the SOAH Administrative Law Judges to GRANT proper and full relief to any newly identified affected property owners, who were not previously notified of the application, in accordance with 16 Tex. Admin. Code 22.52.(a).(5).

Date Signed: June 2, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
John M. Burrow
By:   /s/   John M. Burrow	
16265 Cedar Valley Road
Salado, Texas 76571
Telephone: (254) 702-2452
Email: delmer111821@gmail.com
